---
title: "SHAP dependence plots for the aligned Big Five scores"
output: html_document
---

# SHAP dependence plots for the aligned Big Five scores

This script gives the following figure: Supplementary Figure S5, SHAP Dependence Plots for the Aligned Big Five Scores in the Neural Network. It reads the SHAP values and the hold-out predictor values with standardised aligned scores saved by the neural network script.

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(shapviz)
library(patchwork)

# The saved SHAP values and the hold-out predictor values with standardised aligned scores are loaded.
nnet_trait_shap_values <- readRDS("nnet_trait_shap_values.rds")
nnet_trait_shap_data_standardised <- readRDS("nnet_trait_shap_data_standardised.rds")
```

## Panels and sizes

```{r}
# These are the five panels. Their order is the order of the panels, and the names are the panel titles.
trait_panel_labels <- c(
  CON = "Conscientiousness",
  AGR = "Agreeableness",
  OPE = "Openness",
  EXT = "Extraversion",
  NEU = "Neuroticism"
)

# This factor scales the size of all points and the thickness of all lines in the panels.
nnet_trait_mark <- 7.5 / 12
```

## Drawing the original dependence plot

```{r}
# shapviz draws the original dependence plot: one panel for each aligned score.
# Each grey, semi-transparent point is one hold-out participant, with its SHAP value on the y-axis.
# The x-axis uses the hold-out scores standardised with the training-set mean and standard deviation.
# The points are not coloured by another predictor.
nnet_trait_dependence <- sv_dependence(
  shapviz(nnet_trait_shap_values, X = nnet_trait_shap_data_standardised),
  v = names(trait_panel_labels),
  color_var = NULL,
  color = "grey70",
  share_y = FALSE,
  alpha = 0.45,
  size = 0.6 * nnet_trait_mark
)
```

## Adjusting the plot

```{r}
# The original plot is then adjusted.
nnet_trait_dependence <- nnet_trait_dependence &
  # A black horizontal line is drawn at a SHAP value of zero.
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.6 * nnet_trait_mark) &
  # The x-axis is divided into ten intervals. In each interval, a vertical bar spans the mean SHAP value plus and minus one standard deviation.
  stat_summary_bin(
    fun = mean,
    fun.min = function(y) mean(y) - sd(y),
    fun.max = function(y) mean(y) + sd(y),
    geom = "errorbar",
    bins = 10,
    width = 0.25,
    linewidth = 0.5 * nnet_trait_mark
  ) &
  # A black line connects the mean SHAP values of the ten intervals.
  stat_summary_bin(aes(group = 1), fun = mean, geom = "line", bins = 10, linewidth = 0.5 * nnet_trait_mark) &
  # A black point marks the mean SHAP value of each interval.
  stat_summary_bin(fun = mean, geom = "point", bins = 10, size = 1.5 * nnet_trait_mark) &
  # All panels use the same axes: standardised scores from -4.45 to 4.45 on the x-axis and SHAP values from -0.6 to 0.6 on the y-axis.
  # The x-axis title is removed from the panels, because one title is placed below the whole figure.
  # The panels have a white background, dashed horizontal grid lines, black axis text, and centred titles.
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-4, 4, by = 2), expand = expansion(add = 0)) &
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.5, 0.5, by = 0.25), limits = c(-0.6, 0.6)) &
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-4.45, 4.45)) &
  labs(x = NULL) &
  theme_bw(base_size = 11, base_family = "Arial") &
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey80", linetype = "dashed"),
    axis.ticks = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
    axis.ticks.length = unit(0.15, "cm"),
    axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"),
    axis.title = element_text(colour = "black", face = "plain", size = 11),
    plot.title = element_text(colour = "black", face = "plain", size = 11, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.margin = margin(5, 8, 2, 4)
  )

# Each panel receives the name of its trait as its title.
dependence_panels <- lapply(seq_along(trait_panel_labels), function(i) {
  nnet_trait_dependence[[i]] + labs(title = trait_panel_labels[[i]])
})

# This theme removes the y-axis numbers, ticks, and title. It is applied to neuroticism, so the lower row shows the y-axis only beside extraversion.
hide_y <- theme(
  axis.text.y = element_blank(),
  axis.title.y = element_blank(),
  axis.ticks.y = element_blank()
)

# The upper row contains conscientiousness, agreeableness, and openness. The y-axis is shown once, on the left of this row.
top_row <- dependence_panels[[1]] + dependence_panels[[2]] + dependence_panels[[3]] +
  plot_layout(nrow = 1, widths = c(1, 1, 1), axes = "collect")

# The lower row contains extraversion and neuroticism, centred between two empty spaces.
# The widths give these panels the same width as the panels above.
bottom_row <- plot_spacer() +
  dependence_panels[[4]] +
  (dependence_panels[[5]] + hide_y) +
  plot_spacer() +
  plot_layout(nrow = 1, widths = c(0.326, 1, 1, 0.326), axes = "collect")

# The x-axis title is created as a separate text element.
x_title <- wrap_elements(
  full = grid::textGrob(
    "Standardised aligned Big Five score",
    gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 11, fontfamily = "Arial", col = "black")
  )
)

# The upper row, the lower row, and the x-axis title are stacked. The title occupies a narrow strip at the bottom.
nnet_trait_dependence <- top_row / bottom_row / x_title +
  plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1, 0.045))

# The figure is shown in the R output.
nnet_trait_dependence
```

## Saving the figure

```{r}
# The figure is saved as the PDF for Supplementary Figure S5.
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)

ggsave(
  "figures/figure_shap_trait_dependence_nn.pdf",
  plot = nnet_trait_dependence,
  width = 19.05,
  height = 13.72,
  units = "cm",
  device = cairo_pdf
)
```
